reason: The cited evidence shows that adding boron to HfMoNbTaTiZr formed borides at grain boundaries and improved ductility, and that precipitation strengthening is a general strategy to overcome the strength–ductility trade-off. However, none of the cited passages involve the WTaTiVZr alloy or demonstrate that the proposed mechanism governs its plastic strain and toughness; the extrapolation to this specific system is unsupported.
premises: Fine precipitates at grain boundaries can be formed by adding minor alloying elements to refractory high-entropy alloys.
Such grain-boundary precipitates can improve grain-boundary cohesion and ductility in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys.
Precipitation-strengthened heterostructures can overcome the strength–ductility trade-off in high-entropy alloys.
The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy can be modified by minor alloying additions to form grain-boundary precipitates.
